title: Test-vector suite — small known permanents + 1k-random cross-check
description:
Land a test-vector suite covering hand-checked small permanents and a 1000-sample random cross-check between `permanent_ryser` (T7), `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8), and `permanent_bipedal3` (T9).

## Background

The epic-level success criterion 2 demands `permanent_bipedal3` produce values bit-identical to `permanent_ryser` over `Fp<3>` on 1000 random matrices for $n \in \{1, \ldots, 16\}$ and 100 random matrices for $n \in \{20, 24, 28, 32\}$. T9 carries that test internally; this issue adds the broader vector suite that all three implementations share, plus hand-checked small cases against pen-and-paper computations.

The hand-checked cases are: $1 \times 1$ identity; $2 \times 2$ all-ones; $3 \times 3$ $(-1, 0, 1)$ matrices with known permanents from the paper or pen-and-paper; and $4 \times 4$ permutation matrices.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `crates/gf2-algebra/tests/permanent_vectors.rs` integration test exists.
- [ ] [hard] At least 12 hand-checked small-$n$ cases ($n \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$) compare all three implementations against literal expected values.
- [ ] [hard] Random cross-check: 1000 random matrices for each $n \in \{4, 8, 12, 16\}$; all three implementations agree on every case.
- [ ] [hard] Random cross-check at larger $n \in \{20, 24, 28, 32\}$ on 100 matrices; T7 (oracle) vs T9 (fast path) agreement.
- [ ] [hard] Tests use a fixed RNG seed for determinism; same seed produces identical input matrices across CI runs.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes; per-test wall-clock under 5 s.

## Amendment 2026-05-11 (user-approved, Option A — mirror T9 amendments + tier split)

The original criteria 3, 4, and 6 are mutually inconsistent with T9 (`b0857ae9`)'s amended scope and with the project's nextest budget. The user-approved correction below aligns T11 with the rest of W2.

**Amended criterion 3 (default-tier random cross-check):** Random cross-check: 1000 random matrices for each $n \in \{4, 8, 12\}$ (default tier — each per-$n$ test fits under the 5 s/test budget); 1000 random matrices for $n = 16$ (slow tier, `#[ignore = "sim: ..."]`). All three implementations (`permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>`, `permanent_mod3_reference`, `permanent_bipedal3`) agree on every case. Default-tier passes under `--profile ci`; slow tier passes under `--profile slow --run-ignored ignored-only`.

**Amended criterion 4 (large-$n$ random cross-check):** For $n \in \{20, 24\}$ — 100 random matrices each, slow tier (`#[ignore = "sim: ..."]`). Oracle: `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8) via transitivity through T8's $n \le 12$ bit-identical cross-check vs `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (T7). $n \in \{28, 32\}$ dropped as computationally infeasible — see T9 and epic 2026-05-10 amendments. Per-$n$ slow-tier tests fit the 120 s/test slow-tier budget.

**Amended criterion 6 (test-tier budget):** `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes; **default-tier** per-test wall-clock under 5 s. Slow-tier tests are `#[ignore = "sim: ..."]`-marked and run under `--profile slow` with 120 s/test budget; not exercised by `--profile ci`.

Approved by user 2026-05-11 (epic ae82bd73 session 4, AskUserQuestion option A on T11 amendments).
